thread:
anya: quick sanity run on Sora-Lite v2 (q4_0 with QAT) — small multilang eval.
li-zhang: saw a BLEU delta on zh/ja vs fp16 baseline, about -2.1 on zh. interestingly en unchanged.
sam: can you paste the command you ran?
anya: sure
anya: ```
# repro
python eval.py --model sora-lite-v2 --weight-file sora-lite-v2-q4_0-qat.pt --langs zh,ja,en,ar --seed 42 --batch 64 --prefix-cache
```
marco: what metric suite? sacrebleu or our internal translate-eval?
anya: sacrebleu + locale-aware detok (we used detok-v2 with normalize_spaces=false)
anya: quick numbers (sacrebleu): en: 28.6 -> 28.5, ja: 19.2 -> 17.8, zh: 24.3 -> 22.2
ml-ci-bot: CI note: saw tokenization mismatch warnings for 1.9% of zh examples (non-empty warnings)
li-zhang: tokenization mismatch = different token boundaries vs baseline? can you show an example?
anya: yep
anya: "原文：今天,我们去公园。" baseline tokens: ["今天", ",", "我们", "去", "公园", "。"]
anya: quant tokens: ["今天,我们", "去", "公园。"] <-- merged comma with previous Han chunk
sam: that looks like ZWSP/normalization issue. Did QAT change tokenization? shouldn't.
marco: QAT shouldn't touch tokenizer. maybe runtime detok or locale-normalizer changed between builds.
sre-ops: tagging infra: did the container image change config for icu/normalizer?
anya: image hash is sha256:abcd1234; baseline was abcd0000. small diff in python package icu (PyICU 2.8 -> 2.9)
li-zhang: PyICU bump could change grapheme cluster segmentation in edge cases. Also check our tokenizer glue layer (preserve_punct=True/False)
anya: quick hack: re-run with explicit tokenizer param: --tokenizer-preserve-punct true
anya: re-run results: zh delta shrinks to -0.4 (24.1 vs 24.3), ja still -1.1
sam: ja drop may be different cause (kana-kun separation). Any change in sentencepiece model or merge rules?
anya: same spm model file, identical checksum. but token counts differ slightly: avg tokens per zh sentence: baseline 38.1, q4_0 36.9
marco: lower tokenization length -> fewer tokens -> different attention distribution with cached kv? might affect long-context translations.
li-zhang: Another angle: quant kernel fused attention numeric noise for medium-length sequences. Can we run float fallback on decoder to test? i.e., run with --attn-float-fallback decoder
anya: ran that: ja recovered half the gap (17.8 -> 18.5), zh unchanged. so ja sensitivity tied to attention kernel precision.
ml-ci-bot: Note: A/B run queued: 1743999111-compare-kernel-fallback
sam: plan: 1) pin PyICU back to 2.8 and re-run tokenization smoke; 2) run kernel fallback ablation for attn/ffn; 3) sample perplexity and model logits diff for ja/zh examples; 4) bisect between q4_0 build commits for potential tokenizer glue change.
marco: for bisect, try minimal reproducer: single example ja case where attention changes output. post logits diffs as small TSV.
anya: making reproducer now. also throwing in an eval with token-level alignment to see if merge shows in training-set frequency.
anya: small note: saw bracket flip in arabic with q4_0 on some dev examples: "(مرحبا)" -> ")مرحبا(" in outputs. probably bidi handling in detok.
li-zhang: bidi bracket flip often detok-side. check cldr bidi mirrored chars handling and our rev_map.
sam: ok will open a follow-up thread for the RTL bracket issue if detok pin fixes don't help.
marco: nice triage. if PyICU pin fixes majority, recommend vendor patch in runtime image and re-run full smoke before promote.
anya: thanks — pushing the three runs now. will update this thread with minimal reproducer and logs.
sre-ops: FYI rolling a test image with icu pinned available at gcr.io/redwood/test-images:sora-q4-icu2.8
anya: perfect, will use that.
anya: quick emoji: :work_in_progress:
